answer.evidence: The required_memory_refs are A.txt and B.txt, so the preferred pair is the other two letters, C and D (radon/metrics.py and radon/visitors.py). That gives them 40 of the 60 minutes. I only searched the repo and did not read any of the four files in full. The code the request describes is in radon/raw.py (A). `_find(tokens, token, value)` at raw.py:72 loops over `enumerate(reversed(tokens))` at line 76, which finds the rightmost match. It ends with `raise ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')` at line 79 when there is no match. I gave A 15 minutes so the reverse-index arithmetic and the callers' handling of that ValueError get checked. B (complexity.py) only has an unrelated ValueError at line 41, so it gets 5 minutes. C and D got 20 minutes each as the preferred pair. I haven't checked whether they use `_find`, so those 40 minutes are an allocation choice, not something I found in the code. The same search returned no other `_find` or `reversed` hits in radon/ apart from cli/__init__.py:357 and cli/tools.py:123, which look unrelated.
